title: Implement a HashMap
description: Hash table with separate chaining. Each bucket is an array of [key, value] entries. Hashing: Knuth's multiplicative hash for ints, djb2-style for strings, both modulo capacity. put updates in place if the key exists; otherwise appends. get/has/remove walk the bucket linearly — O(1) average with a decent hash.

notes: Use `>>> 0` to coerce a 32-bit hash to an unsigned int before modulo — otherwise negative numbers give negative bucket indices.
put must SEARCH the bucket first to update an existing key in place. Without that, duplicates accumulate and size lies.
Knuth's multiplier 2654435761 = floor(2^32 / phi) — good distribution for sequential integer keys.

options: Each bucket holds a list of colliding entries
Probing the next slot until empty
Doubling the table on every collision

questions.q: Why must put walk the bucket before appending?
options: To update the value in place when the key already exists — otherwise duplicates leak

questions.q: Purpose of `>>> 0` in the hash function?
options: Coerces to an unsigned 32-bit int so modulo yields a non-negative bucket
Marks the value as a primitive

exercises.prompt: Fill in put and get so an existing key is updated in place rather than duplicated.

L3.prompt: Build HashMap with put/get/has/remove/size. Insert (1,'a'), (2,'b'), (17,'c'); log get(1), get(2), get(17), get(99), has(2); put(2,'B') then log get(2), size; remove(1), log has(1), size.

hints: Each bucket is an array of [k, v] pairs; iterate to find a matching key.
put: if key exists, overwrite the value and return; otherwise push a new pair and bump size.
Use `>>> 0` to keep the hash unsigned before mod-ing by capacity.
